items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S881

SPONSOR: YOUNG
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the highway law, in relation to designating a portion of
the state highway system as the "Private Charles S. Cooper, Jr. Memorial
Highway"

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

Designates State Route 60 in the City of Jamestown, County of Chautau-
qua, as the "Private Charles S. Cooper, Jr. Memorial Highway."

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends the highway law by adding a new section 344-h, which
designates State Route 60 in the City of Jamestown, county of Chautau-
qua, as the "Private Charles S. Cooper, Jr. Memorial Highway."

Section 2: States that the commissioner of transportation shall provide
for the installation and maintenance of adequate signing of the state
highway systems as designated pursuant to section 1 of this act. The
designation will be for ceremonial purposes only, and the roads official
name will not be changed as a result of this act.

Section 3: Provides that the act shall take effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Private Charles S. Cooper, Jr. served his nation in Iraq assigned to the
United States Army's 2nd Battalion, 14th Infantry Regiment, 2nd Brigade
Combat Team, 10th Mountain Division (Light Infantry) Fort Drum, New
York. Private Cooper tragically lost his life in service to our country
on April 29, 2005 after an improvised explosive device (IED) detonated
while he was on patrol in Baghdad, Iraq. Only weeks earlier, on April
12, 2005, Private Cooper had received the Purple Heart Medal after being
injured by shrapnel from another IED in Iraq.  In addition to the Purple
Heart, Private Cooper received the Army Service Ribbon, the Global War
on Terrorism Expeditionary Medal, the National Defense Service Medal,
the Army Good Conduct Medal, the Iraq Campaign Medal, the Combat Infan-
try Badge, and a Bronze Star.

Private Cooper was born on February 29, 1986 and was a lifelong resident
of Chautauqua County and a 2004 graduate of Jamestown High School,
enlisting in the Army four days after graduation. The Chautauqua County
Legislature has expressed its desire to honor Private Cooper. The Chau-
tauqua County Legislature, by unanimous vote, adopted a formal resol-
ution requesting this legislation. The dedication of State Route 60 in
the City of Jamestown is but one small way for this state to honor the
bravery, dedication and ultimate sacrifice of this brave American hero.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2018: S.8852/A.10974 Passed Senate

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None
 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
